text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Lucien Bouchard to join trade mission: Quebec premier separates job creation from sovereignty to participate in trip to Asia.
- Zaire mission back on track: Food drops win tentative support.
- Toronto residents oppose megacity, poll finds: Survey for mayors backs referendum.
- Faculty resorts to rare university strike: Small Ontario school is shut down for the second time in five years.
- Fallen Salinas haunts Dublin incognito: Suspected in Mexico, the once popular leader lives in exile, savouring Irish beer and literature.
- Placer Dome in $600 million shuffle: Gold mining giant launches two takeover bids to consolidate Asia-Pacific operations.
- Hong Kong group buys Canada's biggest hotel: Asian trend continues with deal for Toronto's Delta Chelsea.
- Canadian Airlines peddling regional servers to cut costs, free up planes: Airline targets Central Canada routes.
- Scotiabank newest billionaire: Puts almost $1.07-billion on bottom line, up 22 percent.
- Canadian Airlines gets $140 million break: Transport Minister David Anderson says it's 'the beginnings of a deal,' but stresses all six unions must agree to the restructuring package.
- Gulf Canada tries to chase gas firms from oilsands.
